body:
Split out of task:5d91514e330169b3 (review run 1be93e49b144889f, item 1). The two test modules `extract::rust::tests` and `extract::rust::merge::tests` still live at `src/extract/rust/tests.rs` and `src/extract/rust/merge/tests.rs`, not at their D-206 paths (`<module>_tests.rs` beside the module's file). Deleting and recreating them would lose their symbol IDs and history, and `extract` can't do it safely (see the work run note on that task).

## Need
A store-aware way to move a Rust module's file to a new path in the same crate. The module path and every symbol ID in it stay the same.

## What it does
- Updates the module's stored file and folder (`ModuleRow.file`, `dir`, `owns_dir`).
- Adds or changes the parent's `#[path = "..."]` line on the `mod` declaration.
- Records the old file and the undo state so the task's change can be reviewed and undone like any other.
- Refuses before anything changes when the new path is taken, is outside the crate, or the module isn't Rust.

Agents call it, so it needs a decision in DECISIONS.md and an entry in `src/reference.txt`. The command's name and shape are the worker's to propose in that decision.

## Then use it
Move `extract::rust::tests` to `src/extract/rust_tests.rs` and `extract::rust::merge::tests` to `src/extract/rust/merge_tests.rs`.

## Check
- `files src/extract` lists no `tests.rs`.
- `refs extract::rust::tests.a_child_glob_keeps_its_parents_imports` shows the same ID as before the move.
- `check --warnings` is clean; `run rust-unit` passes.

## Not included
Gleam, moving to another crate or project, and renaming the module path itself.
title: rust: move a module's file, keeping IDs
